name: How much space does an accessible bathroom need for wheelchair turning?

mainEntity.name: What clear floor space and turning room should be planned into an accessible bathroom remodel?
mainEntity.text: What clear floor space and turning room should be planned into an accessible bathroom remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The required space depends on how the bathroom will be used, but the room must allow safe movement without forcing sharp turns or awkward transfers. A wheelchair user needs enough clear floor area to approach the toilet, sink, and shower, while someone using a walker may need less room but still benefits from open pathways and wider doorways. In many older Los Angeles homes, the best solution is not chasing a perfect code diagram, but designing around actual mobility needs. That may mean removing a linen closet, changing the door swing, or using a wall-hung vanity to preserve clearance. The most common mistake is focusing on fixtures first and leaving no usable circulation space. A remodel should be measured from the start with the door width, shower entry, sink depth, and transfer side all mapped out.
acceptedAnswer.description: A wheelchair-accessible bathroom usually needs a clear turning area, open approach to the toilet and sink, and enough doorway clearance to enter without tight maneuvering. If the room is too small for a full turning radius, the layout should be customized around transfer method and equipment needs.
